$description: Canonical record of every dated regulatory event. Instruments reference these by ID rather than carrying their own copies of dates. Enforcement actions live in enforcement.json and are merged into calendar views by reference, not duplicated here.
$note: event_type is mandatory and distinguishes entry into force from application, transposition, compliance and reporting deadlines, delegated and implementing acts, guidance, designation, judicial events and reviews. date_precision records how precisely the date is published: a month-only event is stored as the first of that month. AUDIT-2026-09-25 (2026-09-26): records re-read individually against their sources carry that date in their own last_verified; this file's $last_verified is deliberately unchanged, because the file as a whole was not re-read, and moving it would assert that it was.

events.obligation: Member States must have transposed the CER Directive.
events.verification_note: Art. 26(1): 'By 17 October 2024, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive'; they apply them from 18 October 2024. events.obligation: Member States must have transposed NIS2 into national law.
events.required_action: For entities: the operative compliance date is the national one, which varies by Member State and in several cases has not yet arrived.

events.obligation: The Commission sends letters of formal notice to 23 Member States for failure to fully transpose NIS2.

events.obligation: DORA becomes applicable, with no transposition patchwork.
events.required_action: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party risk arrangements in place.

events.obligation: Article 5 prohibitions and the AI-literacy obligations become applicable.
events.required_action: Cease any prohibited practice; ensure staff AI literacy.
events.verification_note: Verified 27 Sep 2026 against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as published in the Official Journal (OJ L of 12.7.2024), read on 27 Sep 2026 from the Publications Office's Cellar (CELEX 32024R1689): Article 113, third paragraph, point (a) — "Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025". Chapter I holds Articles 1 to 4 (scope, definitions, AI literacy), so Articles 2, 3 and 4 are linked here; Chapter II is Article 5. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (OJ L of 24.7.2026, CELEX 32026R1744, read the same day), Article 1, point (40)(a), keeps this date and carves out only the new Article 5(1)(ba) and (bb), which apply from 2 December 2026. Previously: "Date stated by the brief; not confirmed against the consolidated text in this build."

events.obligation: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice is finalised. It is voluntary.
events.required_action: Consider adherence. The Code supplies the operative detail behind Articles 53 and 55, which are drafted at a high level of abstraction.

events.obligation: General-purpose AI obligations and the governance structures become applicable.
events.required_action: GPAI providers: technical documentation, downstream information pack, copyright policy, public training-content summary. Systemic-risk models additionally owe Art. 55.
events.verification_note: Verified 27 Sep 2026 against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as published in the Official Journal (OJ L of 12.7.2024), read on 27 Sep 2026 from the Publications Office's Cellar (CELEX 32024R1689): Article 113, third paragraph, point (b) — "Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101". Articles 51, 53 and 55 are in Chapter V and Article 99 in Chapter XII, so all four are linked here; Article 101 is not, and applies from the general date. Previously: "Date stated by the brief; not confirmed against the consolidated text in this build."

events.obligation: General application: Chapter III data-access, Chapter IV unfair terms, Chapter VI switching.

events.obligation: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2050 on data access enters into force, establishing a centralised DSA Data Access Portal, procedural safeguards and platform data catalogues.
events.required_action: Designated platforms must publish data catalogues and process vetted-researcher requests through the portal.

events.obligation: The Commission publishes the Digital Omnibus, split into COM(2025) 836 on AI and COM(2025) 837 on data.
COM(2025) 837 final published. A proposal, not law.
Commission review report under Art. 53, COM(2026) 178 final. The statutory deadline was 3 May 2026.
The Commission publishes the European Technological Sovereignty Package, whose centrepiece is the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, COM(2026) 502 final. A proposal, not law.
The Commission reaches a preliminary position that Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure should be designated as gatekeepers. Preliminary only: no designation decision is adopted on this date.
events.verification_note: A preliminary position, not a designation.

events.obligation: The Commission refers Ireland, Spain, France and the Netherlands to the Court of Justice for failing to transpose NIS2, requesting financial sanctions consisting of a lump sum and daily penalties until complete transposition is notified.
The Commission fines Google EUR 890 million for DMA non-compliance in Search and Google Play, and orders compliance within 60 days.
events.required_action: Google to bring the designated core platform services into compliance within the period set by the decision.

events.obligation: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 enters into force, amending the AI Act.

The AI Act's general date of application. Article 101 also applies from this date: the Commission may fine providers of general-purpose AI models up to 3% of annual worldwide turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher (GPAI obligations themselves have applied since 2 August 2025).
events.verification_note: Resolved as to the date. The Commission confirms 2 August 2026 as the general date of application and began enforcing the transparency obligations on that date. What the AI Omnibus moved out of this tranche is recorded on the Omnibus records rather than here. Art. 101 added on 2026-09-26 (audit T-29): Art. 113(b) applies Chapter V from 2 August 2025 'with the exception of Article 101', read from an unofficial explorer of the amended text, not the Official Journal. The audit proposed a separate event; the validator allows one application event per instrument and date, so it is recorded here. Confirmed 27 Sep 2026 against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as published in the Official Journal (OJ L of 12.7.2024), read on 27 Sep 2026 from the Publications Office's Cellar (CELEX 32024R1689): Article 113, second paragraph — "It shall apply from 2 August 2026" — and point (b)'s exception for Article 101, which until then rested on the unofficial explorer.

events.obligation: Commission's target for concluding the AWS and Azure gatekeeper market investigations (within 12 months of their 18 November 2025 opening) — a target, not a legal deadline.
events.required_action: If AWS and Azure are designated, Amazon and Microsoft would have six months to bring those services into compliance with the DMA obligations.
events.verification_note: The date is derived, not published: IP/25/2717 says the Commission 'aims to conclude' within 12 months of 18 November 2025, hence November 2026 at month precision. It is an administrative target, not a deadline in the Regulation. A preliminary position in favour of designation was reached on 25 June 2026 (IP/26/1444). requires_verification cleared on 2026-09-26 by the author's decision: the date and its status as a target both come from the Commission's own press release.

events.obligation: The new Article 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb) prohibitions — AI systems generating or manipulating non-consensual intimate imagery of an identifiable person, and material within Article 2(c) and (e) of Directive 2011/93/EU — together with the new Article 5(1a) and (1b), apply from this date. They were inserted into the AI Act by the Digital Omnibus on AI.
events.required_action: Do not place on the market, put into service or use an AI system within the new Article 5(1)(ba) or (bb) prohibitions from this date.
events.verification_note: Split on 27 Sep 2026. This record used to carry two different things that fall on the same date: an application date and a transitional deadline. It now carries only the application of the new Article 5 prohibitions, verified against Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital Omnibus on AI), Official Journal text read on 27 Sep 2026 from the Publications Office's Cellar (CELEX 32026R1744): Article 1, point (40)(a), replaces Article 113, third paragraph, point (a), so that Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025 "with the exception of Article 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b) which shall apply from 2 December 2026"; Article 1, point (7), inserts those points. The transitional deadline is tl-ai-act-2026-12-02-transition-end. Previously corrected 26 Sep 2026 on the basis of Hunton's and NicFab's secondary accounts, which the primary text now confirms.

events.obligation: The revised Product Liability Directive applies to products placed on the market or put into service after this date. Software and AI fall within strict product liability.
events.required_action: Reassess liability exposure for software and AI-enabled products.
events.verification_note: The brief's Annex A gives only 'Dec 2026'. The precise date of 9 December 2026 comes from Art. 2(1) of Directive (EU) 2024/2853 as recorded in the OJ.

events.obligation: Commission's target for publishing the final report of the sector-wide cloud market investigation (within 18 months of its 18 November 2025 opening) — a target, not a legal deadline.

events.obligation: End of a transitional period, not an application date. Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content that were placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with Article 50(2) machine-readable marking by this date. For systems placed on the market from 2 August 2026, Article 50 already applies.
